result.summary: This PR changes btcsignals::connection::disconnect() to eagerly destroy the associated callback object (or as soon as an in-flight invocation finishes) instead of leaving it alive until an unrelated future connect() call garbage collects it. It adds characterization tests pinning the old and new destruction timing, and includes a follow-up commit adding a fallback for atomic shared_ptr operations on platforms lacking the C++20 feature. The change restores boost::signals2-like semantics for callback lifetime.
result.problem: Previously, disconnected callbacks in btcsignals stayed alive indefinitely, which caused a deadlock on GUI shutdown in the multiprocess bitcoin project (#10102): node notification callbacks own mp::EventLoopRef references that kept the node process from exiting because they weren't freed on disconnect.

result.card: This PR changes btcsignals::connection::disconnect() to eagerly destroy the disconnected callback object instead of leaving it alive until a later unrelated connect() call garbage collects it, restoring boost::signals2-like lifetime semantics. It fixes a real deadlock on GUI shutdown in the multiprocess bitcoin project (#10102), where undestroyed node notification callbacks held IPC proxy references that blocked the node process from exiting, per the CI failure link in the description. A third commit adds a fallback for atomic shared_ptr operations on platforms lacking the C++20 feature, addressing observed build failures on macOS, FreeBSD, and sanitizer CI builds. Reviewer maflcko engaged positively but noted no urgency since the affected consumer (#10102) is unmerged, and the author agreed while suggesting further simplifications; there are no unresolved objections. The PR is reviewable now with no blocking issues, and its priority stems mainly from being a correctness fix to a shared primitive that unblocks other multiprocess work rather than an urgent current-release need.
